chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever prays over a woman, let him not stand in her middle, but rather in what faces her chest; and when he prays over a man, let him stand in his middle.'

And there is no contradiction between these two narrations, because the first hadith said 'if he is a man, at his chest,' meaning the middle, because one expresses a thing by the name of what adjoins it; and similarly in his saying 'if the woman is at her head,' because the head is close to the chest, so it is permissible to express it by it; and this also confirms what we mentioned, what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Where should the Imam stand during the funeral prayer for a woman versus a man?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the jurisprudential distinction in the Imam’s standing position during *Salat al-Janazah*, placing him at the chest for women and the center for men, reflecting subtle differences in ritual etiquette. The text resolves apparent contradictions by noting that 'chest' and 'head' are often used interchangeably in Arabic to denote the central upper body, thereby harmonizing the reports. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on precise physical alignment during communal prayers, linking the leader’s position to the deceased’s spiritual orientation.
